title: No, none (of) and not any
subtitle: There's none left.
summary: Use no and none (of) as the emphatic alternative to not a / not any, and choose a singular or plural noun after no.

left.label: not a / not any - neutral
examples: He **didn't have any** of the usual symptoms.

right.label: no / none (of) - more emphatic
examples: He had **none** of the usual symptoms.

lesson.heading: Other pairs that work the same way
lesson.text: Several other negative words come in the same neutral / emphatic pairs.

examples.text: There isn't anyone / anybody here. and There's **no one** / **nobody** here.
She wasn't anywhere to be seen. and She was **nowhere** to be seen.
Why don't you ever call me? and Why do you **never** call me?

lesson.heading: Not at the start of a clause
lesson.text: We don't usually use *not a / any, not anyone, not anything* in initial position in a sentence or clause, or straight after **and, but** or **that** at the beginning of a clause. We use **no, none of, no one, nothing** instead.

examples.text: **No force** was needed to make them move.
Most players are under 16 and **none of them** is over 20.
I'm sure that **nothing** can go wrong.

lesson.heading: not a in a formal or literary style
lesson.text: In formal or literary writing we *can* use **not a** in initial position, or after *and, but* or *that*.

examples.text: **Not a sound** came from the room.
examples.note: less formally There wasn't a sound from the room.

examples.text: She kept so quiet that **not a soul** in the house knew she was there.

lesson.heading: A singular or plural noun after no?
lesson.text: After **no** we can often use either, with little difference in meaning; the singular is usually more formal. But we use a **singular** noun where we would expect only one of something, and a **plural** noun where we would expect more than one.

examples.text: We want to go to the island but there are **no boats** to take us.
examples.note: or more formally ... there is no boat.

examples.text: I phoned Sarah at home, but there was **no answer**.
He seems very lonely at school, and has **no friends**.

lesson.heading: Extra emphasis
lesson.text: We can give special emphasis to *no* or *none of* with **no amount of** + uncountable noun, **not one ... / not a single ...** + singular countable noun, and **not one of ...** + plural noun.

examples.text: The company is so badly managed that **no amount of** investment will make it successful.
**Not one of** the families affected by the noise wants to move.

lesson.heading: Spoken phrases with no
rows: emphatic ways of saying no, or of refusing to believe something
it isn't (or wasn't) difficult to do

lesson.text: Think about how many you would expect: one answer to a phone call, so *there was no answer* - but many friends at school, so *he has no friends*.

exercises.prompt: We left the house as quietly as possible and ___ us.
exercises.explanation: not anyone cannot follow and at the start of a clause, so we use no one / nobody.

options: No force was needed to make them move.
Not any force was needed to make them move.
Any force was not needed to make them move.
exercises.explanation: not any is not used in initial position; no takes its place.

exercises.prompt: Match each emphatic sentence with its less emphatic version.

pairs.left: She was nowhere to be seen.
pairs.right: She wasn't anywhere to be seen.

pairs.left: Why do you never call me?
pairs.right: Why don't you ever call me?
There isn't a train until tomorrow.

exercises.prompt: I found that ___ in the city centre had any rooms left.
exercises.explanation: The subject comes first in the clause, so none of is used rather than not any of.

exercises.statement: I phoned Sarah at home, but there were no answers.
exercises.explanation: I phoned Sarah at home, but there was no answer. We use a singular noun where we would expect only one of something.

exercises.statement: He seems very lonely at school, and has no friends.
exercises.explanation: Correct. We would expect more than one friend, so the plural noun is right.

exercises.prompt: I had to hire a car because there are no ___ on the island.
exercises.explanation: On a whole island we would expect more than one train or bus, so plural nouns.

exercises.prompt: And then when I had a puncture, I discovered there ___ either.
exercises.explanation: A car normally carries one spare tyre, so the singular noun is right.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence in a literary style.
exercises.answer: Not a sound came from the room.
exercises.explanation: not a is possible in initial position in a formal or literary style; less formally, There wasn't a sound from the room.

exercises.prompt: The floor had dirty black marks all over it, and ___ polishing could get it clean.
exercises.explanation: no amount of + uncountable noun gives the negative special emphasis.

exercises.prompt: I made lots of cakes for the party, but ___ the children liked them.
exercises.explanation: not one of + plural noun is the emphatic form of none of.

exercises.prompt: Match each remark with the reply that fits it.
